Subject: Pilot MAP: acceptance criteria & blocker digest (week of 2026-08-02)

Hi Jordan / Alex —

Following our MAP checkpoint today, attached is an updated MAP spreadsheet (MAP_v1.3.xlsx) with the revised evaluation plan and timeline. Highlights below — please review and confirm anything that looks off.

Quick status snapshot:
- Core inference acceptance: At-risk — throughput tests currently failing final SLA for 8k token context.
- Security evidence: In progress — logs and retention notes ready for review.
- Integration: On track for stepwise canary next Thursday (2026-08-05) if blockers resolved.

Action items (owners in parentheses):
1) Provide sample production traces and retention policy snippet to Acme (Olga) — target: 2026-07-30.
2) Re-run batch throughput with KV cache enabled and share results (Ben) — target: 2026-07-31.
3) Finalize acceptance criteria table in MAP and confirm sign-off flow (Rafael / Jordan) — target: 2026-08-02.
4) DocuSign for pilot amendment (Rafael) — target: 2026-08-03.

Acceptance criteria (draft):
- P1 latency: median <= 120ms for 2k tokens under steady-state.
- Throughput: 120 req/min sustained on dedicated config (quantized variant allowed).
- Output fidelity: BLEU/ROUGE benchmarks within 2% of baseline for primary prompts.
- Security: Audit logs for inference requests retained for 90 days and accessible via API.

Blockers we surfaced:
- Observed KV cache incompatibility on Acme's payload pattern (Ben to investigate).
- One integration endpoint returns 500 on long prompts when streaming enabled.

Attached: MAP_v1.3.xlsx (worksheet: acceptance_criteria, timeline), short stub of meeting notes.

Next steps: Ben will post raw test outputs once the cache setting is toggled; Olga will upload the retention extract to the shared Drive link below. Rafael -> please confirm the acceptance criteria table by end-of-week so we can lock the canary window.

Thanks,
Rafael

Otherwise we can still proceed with the planned canary if we see incremental improvement by Tuesday (2026-08-03).

Folks — short update after the KV cache runs this morning. Attached: integration-test-summary.pdf (summary + raw CSV links).

What I did:
- Re-ran the throughput harness with Acme payload sample v3. Enabled KV cache (default parameters) then disabled KV cache to compare. Each run had 600 concurrent connections for 10 minutes.

Findings:
- With KV cache enabled: steady-state throughput 98 req/min, median latency 135ms for 2k tokens — miss on both throughput and latency targets.
- With KV cache disabled: 112 req/min, median latency 125ms — better but still slightly above latency SLO.
- Error mode tied to a streaming flush race on long prompts; root cause identified in our stream flushing path and a fix is in QA branch.

Next steps / revised action items:
- Deploy hotfix to staging for stream flush race (Ben) — ETA: 2026-08-03 10:00 PT.
- Run post-fix throughput tests and publish artifacts to the Drive link (Ben) — ETA: 2026-08-03 14:00 PT.
- Olga to upload retention API curl example to Drive (Olga) — ETA: 2026-07-30 (pending).
- Rafael / Jordan to confirm final acceptance criteria after post-fix runs (Rafael, Jordan) — target: 2026-08-04.

Canary decision: we should be able to proceed with a limited canary on 2026-08-05 if post-fix numbers meet the improved throughput/latency targets (Ben to confirm by end-of-day 2026-08-03).

Thanks — will push the test artifacts as soon as the staging run completes.

Ben
Senior Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
